original_test_intent: Read one Redfish certificate identified under the AccountService ActiveDirectory certificate collection and obtain a human-readable successful response.
original_method: Resolve an advertised CertificateId from the ActiveDirectory Certificates collection, perform one authenticated GET over verified TLS and validate the returned certificate resource without altering directory or certificate state.
manual_activity: Supply the read-only credential handle, trusted CA bundle, validated ActiveDirectory Certificates link and approved certificate evidence-retention policy.
safety_requirements: Do not follow private-key or secret-bearing links
Do not create, replace, renew or delete certificates
Do not change Active Directory configuration
Redact sensitive directory hostnames and certificate identity fields per policy
Do not claim live LDAPS authentication or effective trust from metadata alone
agent_execution_scope: Bind BMC, AccountService and firmware identity
Read ActiveDirectory and its advertised Certificates collection
Use secret-safe credentials and trusted TLS
Validate JSON, schema, identity, public-certificate fingerprint and validity metadata

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The GET path matches the named ActiveDirectory certificate resource, but `-k`, credential exposure, free-form CertificateId and full unredacted output make the command unsafe as written.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover the resource from the advertised ActiveDirectory Certificates collection, then use one verified-TLS GET with a secret-backed read-only credential; capture HTTP status and validate identity, schema, fingerprint and redaction before retaining evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The ActiveDirectory resource, operator-selected CertificateId and 15/10 timing remain; no certificate identity, trust role or expected issuer is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the row as a bounded read-only certificate metadata query whose target identity is derived from the ActiveDirectory collection and whose evidence is schema-validated and redacted.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes log clearing, hardcoded credentials and TLS bypass; adds collection membership, HTTP/JSON/schema/identity/fingerprint validation and explicit no-private-key/no-mutation boundaries.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates one advertised ActiveDirectory certificate resource only; it does not prove that directory authentication succeeds, that LDAPS negotiated this certificate or that the configured trust chain is operational.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Certificate subject, SAN, issuer and directory endpoint data may be sensitive, and firmware schemas may differ; retain only approved public metadata.

project_override_considerations: Use the firmware-advertised ActiveDirectory Certificates link rather than assuming a fixed path when they differ. If the endpoint omits certificate bytes or fingerprints, validate only the schema-defined public fields and report the limitation without requesting private-key material.
expected_evidence: ActiveDirectory Certificates collection URI and selected member identity
Public-certificate fingerprint or explicit schema limitation

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, Criteria and Script all identify a read-only GET of one ActiveDirectory certificate resource; the weak generic Criteria require strengthening but do not contradict that intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The required access, TLS, schema, collection identity and redaction inputs are normal execution-package prerequisites, so the engineering review is complete and the case is not intrinsically blocked.

review_improvement: Converts a credential-exposing TLS-bypassed dump into a collection-bound, secret-safe and schema-validated read of one Active Directory certificate while preventing overclaim of effective directory trust.
independent_technical_reasoning: A certificate object below AccountService/ActiveDirectory can contain directory hostnames or organization identity and may represent a CA or trust anchor, so its public metadata still needs explicit retention controls. CertificateId must come from the advertised AD collection to prevent cross-collection or stale-object substitution. A successful GET proves resource availability and parseable metadata only; it does not prove that LDAP authentication used the certificate, that a remote directory is reachable or that the trust chain is accepted during an LDAPS handshake. Fingerprint and validity checks strengthen object identity without accessing private-key material.
